messages.text:
The first verifier run found a real formatting difference: eza quotes names containing spaces by default, while the port printed them raw.

I also saw Python’s Windows stdout encoding corrupt tree glyphs in the terminal capture, so I’m fixing quoting and forcing UTF-8 output before rerunning the oracle verifier.
